card.title: Salad App & Card
card.subtitle: Helping people understand their credit, take meaningful actions, and build a stronger credit profile over time.

hero.title: Salad App & Card
hero.summary: Salad offers UK loans of £300–£1,500 using Open Banking and affordability checks. They wanted to launch a credit card and complementary financial app to help people understand their credit and take steps to improve their credit history over time.

blocks.html:
Salad already offered Salad Loans, a personal loan product for UK customers. Alongside the lending business, the company had also developed an MVP mobile app using Open Banking to help users understand their spending and financial health.

The opportunity was to evolve this MVP into a broader credit-building experience, particularly for people with low, limited, or damaged credit profiles, including customers who may not qualify for a Salad loan.

The redesigned Salad app brings together financial insights, credit information, personalised guidance, practical credit-building actions, and the new Salad Card to help users strengthen their credit profile over time.

My role was to evolve the existing MVP into a clearer, more actionable experience while designing the new credit and card journeys.

blocks.title: Business goals
items: Extend Salad beyond loans by giving declined applicants a meaningful next step
Increase activation by building trust in Open Banking
Improve long-term engagement throughout the credit-building journey
Grow adoption of the paid Salad Card

blocks.title: Validation metrics
items: Task success across Open Banking, credit tools, and Salad Card application
Drop-off across key onboarding and card flows
User understanding of their credit profile and next steps
User confidence in how the Salad Card works
Overall usability and ease of navigation

blocks.html: The existing MVP mainly showed users what was happening with their money. The new experience needed to help them understand what it means and what they can do next. The strategy was to connect financial and credit information with relevant, personalised guidance and actions. Depending on their situation, users could be guided towards credit-building tools, education, better financial habits, or the Salad Card. This shifted Salad from a data-heavy financial dashboard to a guided credit-building experience that can support users over time.

Salad focuses on three core user groups, including people with low, limited, or damaged credit profiles.

They start from different financial situations, but share a common goal: building a stronger credit profile and improving their future access to financial products.

items.goal: Understand credit and start building a credit profile
items.challenge: Has little or no credit history and may not know where to start

items.goal: Rebuild their profile after previous financial difficulties or life events
items.challenge: Improving credit can take a long time and the actions that help are not always obvious

items.goal: Establish a financial and credit footprint
items.challenge: Limited UK credit history can make mainstream products difficult to access

blocks.html: Across all three groups, users may find credit confusing, feel overwhelmed by financial information, or have concerns about sharing their data. This created a shared design need: make credit easier to understand, build trust, and give users clear, relevant next steps.
The direction was informed by the existing MVP, stakeholder workshops, and previous customer research through interviews.

items.finding: Too much data, not enough meaning. Users saw numbers without clear context or next steps.
items.insight: Prioritised clear insights and actionable next steps.

items.finding: Open Banking requires trust and clear value. Users need a reason to share financial data.
items.insight: Explained the value before asking for consent.

items.finding: Credit building takes time. Progress may take 18–24 months.
items.insight: Designed for ongoing guidance and progress.

items.finding: The secured card concept can be difficult to understand.
items.insight: Used visual, step-by-step explanations: how funding, spending and repayment work
Surfaced relevant guidance and actions based on the user's situation.

blocks.text: Bringing all accounts into one view

blocks.html: I redesigned the account experience so users can securely connect multiple bank accounts and see their finances in one place. The Open Banking journey explains the value of connecting before asking for consent, helping establish trust from the start.
Rather than just showing transactions and balances, I designed insights that help users understand their spending, income, upcoming payments, and patterns across connected accounts.
I integrated credit score and report data into the app, breaking it down into clear factors such as credit usage, accounts, public records, payment history, and score changes over time.

blocks.text: Helping users know what to do next

blocks.html:
I connected credit information with personalised guidance, educational content, and tools that help users explore ways to strengthen their credit profile.

This includes relevant tips, educational content, and a score simulator that lets users explore how different actions could affect their credit.

blocks.text: Making the Salad Card simple to understand and manage

blocks.html: I designed the Salad Card experience from discovery and application through to everyday card management. The experience explains how the secured card works, then gives users clear access to their balance, card details, wallet, security controls, and transactions.

The project is currently in partner selection and technical integration planning, including the services required for Open Banking, credit reporting, and card processing.

The next step is to validate the core journeys with users before implementation and measure whether the experience improves comprehension, confidence, and task completion.

The biggest lesson from this project was that financial information only becomes useful when users understand what it means and what they can do with it.

The most important product decision was moving the experience from showing financial data to guiding users toward relevant actions. That principle shaped the navigation, insights, credit tools, education, and Salad Card experience.

It also helped clarify the role of each Salad product: Salad Loans addresses an immediate borrowing need, while the Salad app and Salad Card support a longer journey toward stronger credit readiness.
